deities: Lord Narasimha (self-manifested swayambhu image on the cave wall, presiding)
Shiva Linga (worshipped by the demon Jalasura, at the cave's end)
festivals: Narasimha Jayanti (likely; not confirmed in the sources consulted — verify)

history.dynasty: Ancient; no dated inscription cited in sources consulted. The Bidar region was successively under the Mauryas, Satavahanas, Kadambas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Bahmanis.
history.period: Antiquity undated; a living pilgrimage site
history.summary: The Narasimha Jhira (Jharni) Cave Temple is excavated in a approx. 300-metre tunnel under the Manichoola hill range, about 4.8-5 km from Bidar city. Devotees wade through 4-5 feet of perennial spring water for the full length of the cave to reach a roughly carved, self-manifested (swayambhu) image of Narasimha on the laterite wall, with a Shiva Linga beside it. Legend says Narasimha, after slaying Hiranyakashipu, killed the demon Jharasura (Jalasura), a devotee of Shiva, in this cave; at the demon's dying request Narasimha took residence here, and the demon's body became the stream that has never dried up. Bats roost in the cave. FLAG: sources conflict on timings (7:00 AM-6:00 PM vs 8:00 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00-5:00 PM with a midday closure) and one source says entry through the water tunnel to the garbhalaya has been restricted since 2019 — verify on the ground before visiting. CSV NOTE: the CSV's 'state' column wrongly holds the town name 'Bidar' — the temple is in the state of Karnataka.

name: Narasimha Jhira Cave Temple
town_description: Bidar is a historic town in northeastern Karnataka, once the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, known for its fort, the Mahmud Gawan madrasa and Bidri metalwork. It lies about 120-140 km from Hyderabad and is the district headquarters of Bidar district.
tradition: Vaishnavism (with a Shaiva presence — a Shiva Linga stands in the cave)

travel.airport: Bidar Airport has no scheduled commercial services; the nearest operational airport is Hyderabad, approx. 120-140 km.
travel.railway: Bidar railway station, approx. 5 km from the temple; Bidar-Hyderabad intercity trains operate.
travel.road: On Malkapur Road, Mangalpet, on the outskirts of Bidar, approx. 5 km from the railway station; reachable by auto or taxi. Carry a full change of clothes and a towel — devotees emerge soaked.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Monsoon swells the cave stream, so water levels can be higher; summers are hot outside the cave.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: reported as 7:00 AM-6:00 PM by one travel guide, but another source gives 8:00 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00-5:00 PM with a midday cleaning closure. VERIFY before visiting. The sanctum fits only about eight people at a time, so expect queues.
